# SIDEREAL OBSERVATIONS

Furthermore (and this is even more wonderful), those stars which have been called **Nebulae** <gloss>misty clouds</gloss> by every astronomer up to this day are in fact groups of stars planted together in a marvelous manner. Although each individual star escapes our vision because of its smallness or its great distance from us, that whiteness arises from the blending of their rays. Thus, what was previously believed to be a denser part of the heavens, capable of reflecting the rays of the stars or the Sun, is actually a collection of stars. We have observed several of these, and we wished to include the **asterisms** <gloss>star patterns</gloss> of two of them.

In the first diagram, you have the **Nebula** called the Head of Orion <note>the region around the star Meissa in the constellation of Orion</note>, in which we have counted twenty-one stars.

The second contains the **Nebula** named **Praesepe** <gloss>The Manger or Beehive Cluster</gloss>, which is not just one star, but a mass of more than forty small stars. Besides the **Aselli** <gloss>The Little Asses; the stars Gamma and Delta Cancri</gloss>, we have noted thirty-six stars arranged in the following order.

<column-break/>

->THE NEBULA PRAESEPE<-

<note>A telescopic star chart depicts the 'Nebulosa Praesepe' (the Beehive Cluster), showing over thirty-six individual stars. The drawing includes the two larger stars known as the Aselli, demonstrating how the telescope resolves what appears as a single misty patch to the naked eye into a dense cluster of distinct stars.</note>

->THE NEBULA OF ORION<-

<note>A telescopic star chart of the 'Nebulosa Orionis' (the Orion Nebula region) displays twenty-one individual stars. This scientific illustration represents one of the first proofs that celestial regions previously classified as nebulae are actually composed of stars.</note>

<summary>Galileo reveals that astronomical nebulae are not clouds of celestial vapor but clusters of stars invisible to the naked eye. He provides detailed star charts of the Orion nebula and the Praesepe cluster to prove his telescopic observations.</summary>
